TTGR63 – Absent Friends Ride

Start: Dalgety Bay Sailing Club · Finish: Tay Bridge Carpark

Distance: 54.1 miles (cycling-route estimate) · Ascent: Not available · Descent: Not available · Difficulty: Moderately Difficult

Scenery and points of interest

The Absent Friends Ride is a special 54.1-mile journey across Fife, bringing Talking Tandems cyclists together for a day of shared memories, companionship and cycling. Starting from Dalgety Bay Sailing Club, the route heads inland through Inverkeithing, Crossgates, Hill of Beath and Cowdenbeath before continuing through Kelty, Lumphinnans and Lochgelly. Passing Cardenden and Auchterderran, the ride travels through communities closely associated with Fife's mining heritage, gradually making its way towards the countryside of central Fife.

From Kinglassie and Thornton, the journey continues through Eastfield, Markinch and Star before reaching Milldeans, Burnturk and Cults Hill. This middle section brings a change of character, with the route passing through rural Fife and the villages of Craigrothie, Ceres and Pitscottie. The changing countryside, with its hills, farmland and smaller settlements, provides a fitting setting for a ride that celebrates friendship and the experiences shared by tandem teams over the years.

The final part of the journey heads north-east through Strathkinness and Edenside towards Guardbridge and Leuchars. Continuing through Pitlethie, Rhynd and Vicarsford, the route approaches Tayport before finishing at the Tay Bridge car park. The River Tay provides a memorable setting for the conclusion of this point-to-point ride. From the Forth to the Tay, the Absent Friends Ride offers an opportunity to enjoy the company of fellow cyclists while remembering friends who are no longer riding alongside us.

Route highlights
  • Dalgety Bay Sailing Club: The familiar starting point for a memorable journey across Fife.
  • Lochgelly, Cardenden and Auchterderran: Communities reflecting central Fife's industrial and mining heritage.
  • Markinch and Star: A transition from the larger settlements towards the rural heart of Fife.
  • Cults Hill, Craigrothie and Ceres: A varied countryside section with changing elevations and traditional Fife villages.
  • Strathkinness, Guardbridge and Leuchars: The north-eastern section of the journey as the route approaches the Tay.
  • Tayport and Tay Bridge: A fitting destination beside the River Tay, bringing this special ride to its conclusion.

Terrain and cycling difficulty

Difficulty: Moderately Difficult

The Absent Friends Ride is a substantial 54.1-mile point-to-point journey from Dalgety Bay Sailing Club to the Tay Bridge car park. Combining the rolling countryside of central Fife with a succession of towns, villages and rural sections, this is a rewarding endurance ride. The distance and accumulated climbing call for steady pacing, good communication and teamwork throughout.

  • Distance: Approximately 54.1 miles (87.1 km). Unlike many Talking Tandems routes, this is a one-way journey, starting at Dalgety Bay Sailing Club and finishing at the Tay Bridge car park. Allow sufficient time for rest stops, refreshments and regrouping.
  • Climbing: Approximately 558 metres of cumulative ascent are estimated. The route climbs away from the Forth coast into central Fife, with further undulations around Kinglassie, Cults Hill, Craigrothie and the countryside approaching Strathkinness.
  • Descending: Approximately 531 metres of cumulative descent are estimated. The route includes several changes in elevation, with notable descents from the higher countryside towards lower-lying areas, particularly on the approach to the Tay.
  • Gradients: Elevations range from approximately sea level to 199 metres. Some shorter uphill sections may approach 7%, requiring timely gear changes and coordinated pedalling from both riders.
  • Route character: The journey links numerous communities, including Cowdenbeath, Lochgelly, Cardenden, Markinch, Ceres, Guardbridge, Leuchars and Tayport. Pilots should be prepared for frequent junctions, changes in direction and a mixture of more settled and rural surroundings.
  • Tandem considerations: The combination of distance and repeated climbs makes energy management particularly important. A comfortable, sustainable pace will help both riders conserve strength for the later stages. Pilots should communicate upcoming climbs, descents and junctions clearly, while regular breaks will give everyone an opportunity to rest and regroup.

Overall: A rewarding, moderately difficult endurance ride crossing Fife from the Forth towards the Tay. With its varied countryside, substantial distance and special significance to Talking Tandems, the Absent Friends Ride is as much about friendship, remembrance and shared experiences as it is about the cycling itself.
